ai.description: The Sind Krait reaches 1.2 meters. It is glossy black with narrow, white crossbands and a distinct vertebral ridge. The head is slightly wider than the neck, and it possesses a rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Sind Krait is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, thin white vertebral line or series of spots, which is absent in the common Indian Krait (*B. caeruleus*).
ai.habitat: The Sind Krait inhabits arid and semi-arid plains, often found in agricultural fields, scrublands, and sandy areas at low to moderate altitudes across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Sind Krait is primarily nocturnal and terrestrial, often emerging after dark to actively hunt other snakes, lizards, and small rodents across its arid habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Sind Krait is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–14 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing between August and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sind Krait (*Bungarus sindanus*) is found in the arid regions of northwestern India, specifically across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and parts of Punjab and Haryana.
